title: Make the provenance hash read the committed blob, not the working tree
question: After the fix, do the Windows and Linux runs produce the same digest for all fourteen manifest entries?
answer: Yes. Hashing `git cat-file -p HEAD:path` (never `git archive`) yields the same sha256 for all 14 contracted command-center paths on an LF commit after the worktree is rewritten to CRLF. Raw working-tree sha256 differs for every file, so the blob-route green is not silence in both states. Two digests were re-derived with `git show`, not cat-file. Windows was simulated by CRLF worktree materialisation on this Linux box, not a native Windows checkout. SENTINEL:IMP-0439:PROVENANCE-BLOB-HASHED

implementation.fallback: LF-normalised working-tree bytes only when the path is not a blob (tmp fixtures, untracked files)

digest_table.taken_on: Linux fixture git repo; Windows checkout simulated by rewriting the worktree to CRLF after an LF commit (core.autocrlf materialisation)

evidence.claim: Blob sha256 is identical for all 14 contracted paths on LF vs CRLF worktrees; recorded provenance hash equals the blob.
Two blob digests re-derived with git show match git cat-file; REACH-6 is silent on CRLF-only and fires on content change; working-tree hash differs from blob after CRLF rewrite.

negative_controls.description: Raw working-tree sha256 must differ from blob sha256 on a CRLF worktree, proving the blob route changed something.
REACH-6 must fire when snapshot content actually changes.
REACH-6 must stay silent on a CRLF-only rewrite of the same blob.
